chunks: "Treat your sick ones with charity, ward off tribulation with du'a, and seek sustenance through charity. For it loosens from between the jaws of seven hundred devils, and there is nothing heavier upon Satan than charity given to a believer. And it falls into the hand of the Lord, Blessed and Exalted, before it falls into the hand of the servant."

key_terms.الدُّعَاءِ: supplication; a means by which tribulation is repelled
key_terms.الرَّبِّ: the Lord; Blessed and Exalted, who receives the charity before it reaches the servant
key_terms.الصَّدَقَةِ: charity; a means of healing, repelling affliction, and drawing sustenance
key_terms.الْبَلَاءَ: tribulation or affliction that is warded off through du'a
key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنِ: the believer; the recipient whose receiving charity is especially weighty against Satan
key_terms.شَيْطَانٍ: devil; the unseen adversary burdened by charity

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام describe the effects of charity and du'a on illness, tribulation, and sustenance?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches the spiritual efficacy of charity and du'a in confronting illness, tribulation, and constriction in sustenance. It emphasizes the immense unseen effect of charity, especially when given to a believer, and its nearness to Allah, tabaraka wa ta'ala.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1730 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:

"Treat your sick ones with charity, ward off tribulations with supplication, and seek sustenance through charity. Charity releases the grip of seven hundred devils. There is nothing heavier on Satan than charity given to a believer. It reaches the hand of the Lord (azj), blessed and exalted, before it reaches the hand of the servant."
